title_en: The Company That Invented Its Own Killer
title_zh: 发明了数码相机，却被它打败
english_paragraphs: In 1975 Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built the first digital camera. The toaster-sized gadget, a cumbersome heavyweight of about eight pounds, was hardly portable, let alone handheld. Its first rudimentary picture held 10,000 black-and-white pixels. Recording it on a cassette took 23 seconds, and a playback unit showed it on a television.

Kodak's revenues showed its dependence on film, the profitable pillar of its business. Technical staffers were appreciative of the camera, but it needed no film. By Sasson's recollection, his superiors at headquarters called it cute and urged him to keep it hushed. A patent followed in 1978. Production never did.

The advent of digital photography proved disruptive. In June 2009 Kodak said it would stop making Kodachrome, its analogue film, citing lessened demand in the digital era. Kodak's manpower had reached an apex of about 145,000 in the 1980s. By 2012, layoffs since 2003 had slashed 47,000 jobs, alongside the shutdown of 13 factories and some 130 labs.

On 19 January 2012 the 131-year-old firm sought Chapter 11 protection from its creditors, sapped by pension costs and years of slowness in going digital. Citigroup, a lender, provided $950 million for its restructuring. A portfolio of 1,100 digital imaging patents fetched about $525 million from a consortium of twelve buyers, including the giants Apple and Google.

After 19 months of reorganisation, the once-mighty Kodak left bankruptcy in September 2013, downsized, streamlined, and refocused as a commercial printer for business clients. In November 2009 President Obama had decorated Sasson with national laurels, commending his digital camera. That medal's year also saw Kodak announce the end of Kodachrome.
chinese_paragraphs: 1975年，柯达工程师史蒂文·萨松造出第一台数码相机。这台烤面包机大小的装置是个约八磅重的笨重大块头，几乎谈不上便携，更不用说手持。它的第一张粗糙照片只有一万个黑白像素；把照片记录到盒式磁带上需要23秒，再由回放装置显示在电视上。
柯达的营收显示，公司依赖胶卷这项利润支柱。技术人员很欣赏这台相机，可它不需要胶卷。据萨松回忆，总部上司说它挺可爱，却让他别声张。1978年，相机取得专利，但这台原型机始终没有投产。
数码摄影的问世带来颠覆性冲击。2009年6月，柯达宣布将停产Kodachrome这一传统胶卷产品，理由是数码时代需求减少。公司员工规模曾在20世纪80年代达到约14.5万人的顶峰。到2012年，自2003年起的裁员已削减4.7万个岗位，同时关闭了13家工厂与约130个冲印实验室。
养老金成本与多年数码转型迟缓不断削弱公司。2012年1月19日，这家拥有131年历史的企业申请美国《破产法》第11章保护，以免债权人追讨。贷款方花旗集团提供9.5亿美元用于重组。包括苹果、谷歌等巨头在内的十二家买方组成财团，以约5.25亿美元买下1100项数字成像专利组成的专利组合。
经过19个月重组，昔日强大的柯达于2013年9月走出破产程序：缩小规模、精简业务，重新聚焦于为企业客户提供商业印刷服务。早在2009年11月，奥巴马总统就授予萨松国家级荣誉，表彰他的数码相机。而在这枚奖章颁发的同一年，柯达也宣布了Kodachrome胶卷的终结。

cover_question: 造出数码相机的公司，为什么仍被数码时代冲击？
reading_note: 史实说明：这是2009年度的国家技术与创新奖章，实际颁发日为2010年11月17日（白宫典礼记录）。柯达宣布停产Kodachrome是在2009年，因此两件事并非发生于同一年。
illustration_prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE-SPECIFIC SCENE: A historically plausible 1975 digital-camera prototype on an engineer workbench, about toaster-sized rather than a modern pocket camera: a boxy open-frame assembly with exposed sage circuit boards, a single black optical lens at the front, and a compact cassette recorder attached to the framework, showing the awkward experimental nature of the first camera. The prototype is the clear focal object. A simple unbranded cassette tape rests nearby, and a softly suggested bulky CRT television in the background shows only a vague monochrome pixelated patch without recognizable letters, numbers, interface or invented charts, recalling the separate playback step. No people are necessary. No modern DSLR, smartphone, LCD camera screen, polished consumer gadget, corporate logo or brand label. Warm ivory workbench light with restrained terracotta wood, tactile matte watercolor and colored-pencil detail. It is an editorial reconstruction of the early apparatus, not an exact engineering schematic or proof of a production model.
approved_summary: 1975年，柯达工程师萨松造出第一台数码相机：约八磅重、一万黑白像素，存一张照片需23秒。
胶卷是利润支柱；据萨松回忆，上司让他别声张。原型机1978年获专利，却未投产。
数码摄影冲击胶卷需求，转型迟缓与养老金负担削弱公司，柯达于2012年申请破产保护。
柯达获9.5亿美元贷款，并以约5.25亿美元出售1100项专利；2013年完成重组，转做企业印刷。
柯达2009年宣布停产Kodachrome胶卷；萨松获2009年度美国国家技术与创新奖章，实际于2010年授勋。
